s3.verdict: A purposeful pull-back that opens tight on the woman's back and broom and settles on the full classroom, expressing her service at its margins; the woman and broom stay coherent together, nothing clips awkwardly, and both the opening and final full-plate frames read well. Dust is a fitting, subtle ambient for a swept morning room and the engraved print style is preserved.
s3.rationale: A quiet beginning before lessons: a Reveal opens tight on the broom and the woman's back, then pulls out to discover the whole classroom she serves but does not yet belong to, while both layers settle slowly together.

s4.verdict: Publishable. The pull-back from the lamplit typewriter and shorthand pad at t=0 to the full two-half composition at t=1 clearly enacts the turning point: study on the left gives way to the woman, seen from behind, walking toward the harbour window, hills and canvas ambulance on the right. Her rightward drift reinforces that crossing without separating her from the ground, the typewriter remains seated on the desk, no doubled edges, ghosts or awkward frame clipping are visible, and the final wide frame is a strong dwell image preserving the hand-coloured engraving style. The light-sweep is fitting for the lamplight subject.
s4.rationale: A quiet beginning of study becomes a turning point: a Reveal opens tight on the typewriter and shorthand desk, then travels out and right across the harbour window to the woman walking toward the hills and ambulance beyond.

s6.verdict: Do not publish as-is. The plate and layer integrity are sound, but the motion is too timid to express the encounter; it reads as a near-static wide shot rather than a reveal from the starving man to the woman at the hotel door.
s6.rationale: A turning-point encounter: a Reveal plus lateral Journey opens tight on the starving man's silhouette in the dark, then travels across and pulls back to discover the woman stopped on the steps before the hotel's warm revolving door.
filmIssues: The intended reveal/journey is barely readable: all six frames show almost the same wide hotel composition, with the starving man still small at the left edge in frame 1, so the opening is not tight on him and the pull-back/travel to the woman does not register as purposeful movement.

First frame is a good wide plate but not the promised close opening on the man; last frame is essentially the same wide picture, so the dwell image gains no new revelation of the woman between light and dark.
Subject coherence is clean: no tearing, doubled edges, haloing, ghosting or awkward frame clipping is visible in the woman or man, and the layers stay in place.

The light-sweep ambient is not noticeably distracting in the stills and fits the warm hotel doorway, and the print texture/style is preserved, but the overall move is no clearer or more expressive than a plain centred push-in/pull-back.
s6.note: best round scored 5, no better than a plain push-in

s7.rationale: A turning-point application: a Reveal opens tight on the fountain pen that wrote her request, then travels up and out to the hospital while the caped woman rises up its steps, undeterred at 47.
filmIssues: The claimed reveal barely happens: at t=0 zoom is only about 1.21, so the pen, envelope and hospital are all already fully readable; the move is a gentle pull-back rather than a tight-on-the-pen opening travelling up to the hospital.
The woman does not rise up the steps. She has no cut-out layer, so she stays fixed to the hospital background in every frame; the rationale's central action is not visible.

Only cut-2 (pen) is given layer motion, and it is very small (drift about 0.011, scale 0.96). The pen stays coherent on the envelope with no obvious tearing, doubled edge or ghost, but its movement is near-imperceptible.

The letter/envelope (cut-1) is absent from the motion plan, so foreground letter and background hospital separate only through the modest camera move; parallax between the application and the institution is weak.

First frame is serviceable but crops the envelope awkwardly at the left/right edges without being a true pen close-up; the last frame is the strongest picture — full plate, clear margins, good to dwell on.

Dust ambient is subtle and era-appropriate, and the woodcut/newsprint style is preserved; no layer clips badly at the end, but the overall film is only slightly more expressive than a plain centred move.

plateDefects.detail: The foreground object reads as a cream/white airmail envelope with red border stripes, not the blue airmail sheet specified in the art direction; the hospital behind is also rendered in the same black ink rather than a distinct sepia.

s10.verdict: Timid pull-back that never actually conceals then reveals its subject — the woman is present from the first frame and her climb does not read.
s10.rationale: A quiet turning point — a home become a ward — told as a Reveal: open tight on the bungalow's lined-up beds, then pull back and down to discover the woman with her tray climbing the steps and the coconut and banana slope around her.
filmIssues: The pull-back is too timid to perform the stated reveal: at t=0 the woman, tray, steps, basket, palms and banana plants are already fully visible, so nothing is discovered as the camera eases from zoom 1.22 to 1.0.
The woman (cut-2, the central figure on the steps despite its 'coconuts' label) barely climbs — its small up-drift reads as parallax, not as a purposeful ascent carrying the tray toward the ward.

First frame is not a tight opening on the lined-up beds and last frame is only a marginally wider version of the same picture, so the move feels close to a plain centred push-in in reverse and would not read clearly in either direction.

No obvious tearing, doubled edges, halo or ghosting is visible in the contact sheet, and no layer clips the frame edge awkwardly; the light-sweep is subtle and does not disturb the 1970s silkscreen print style.
